description: The chart illustrates how perplexity varies across different pruning percentages for two methods, “Per-Output” and “Per-Layer,” shown as paired bars at each percentage. The horizontal axis contains the pruning-rate categories labeled 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80% in increasing order. The vertical axis is labeled “Perplexity” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks at approximately \(10^1\), \(10^2\), and \(10^3\). Each category has two adjacent bars: a blue bar for Per-Output and an orange bar for Per-Layer (as indicated by the legend in the upper-left). At 10% the bars are both near about 5–6 perplexity; at 20% and 30% they remain around roughly 5–6; at 40% they are around ~6–7; at 50% around ~7–8; at 60% around ~9–11; at 70% the blue bar is around ~20 while the orange bar is around ~35–40; and at 80% the blue bar is around ~500 while the orange bar is near ~900–1000. The bars are grouped side-by-side (not stacked), there are no additional annotations on individual bars, and the categories are not sorted by bar height but follow the ascending percentage order.
